title: Chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the amount of a substance?
questions.explanation: The mole is the SI base unit for amount of substance; it counts elementary entities such as atoms or molecules.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many atoms are present in exactly 12 g of carbon-12?
questions.explanation: 12 g of carbon-12 is one mole, which contains Avogadro's number, 6.022 × 10^23, of atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of water are present in 36 g of water? (Molar mass of H2O = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Moles = 36 g / 18 g per mol = 2 mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the mass of 0.25 mol of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CaCO3 is 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g/mol, so 0.25 mol has a mass of 25 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Mole ratio C : H : O = 40/12 : 6.7/1 : 53.3/16 = 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 2 mol of hydrogen gas and 2 mol of oxygen gas are made to react completely according to 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. What mass of water is formed? (H2O = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: 2 mol H2 needs only 1 mol O2, so H2 is the limiting reagent and gives 2 mol of water = 36 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the molality of a solution made by dissolving 18 g of glucose (molar mass 180 g/mol) in 500 g of water?
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 18/180 = 0.1 mol; mass of solvent = 0.5 kg; molality = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 mol per kg.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molarity of a solution prepared by dissolving 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) in water to make 500 mL of solution.
questions.explanation: Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution, so 0.1 mol in 0.5 L gives 0.2 M.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many significant figures are there in the measurement 0.00450 g? Give a reason.
questions.answer: Three significant figures (4, 5 and the final 0).
keyPoints: Trailing zero after a non-zero digit in a decimal number is significant
questions.explanation: Zeros that only locate the decimal point at the start are not counted, but the final zero shows measured precision.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which scientist discovered the atomic nucleus through the gold foil scattering experiment?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment showed that most of the atom's mass and positive charge is in a tiny nucleus.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that the third shell (n = 3) can hold?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of electrons in a shell is 2n^2 = 2 × 9 = 18.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which set of quantum numbers (n, l, ml) is NOT permissible for an electron in an atom?
questions.explanation: For a given n, l can have values 0 to n-1 only, so l = 2 is not possible when n = 2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the ground state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24)?
questions.explanation: Chromium prefers a half-filled 3d subshell, so one 4s electron shifts to 3d, giving [Ar] 3d5 4s1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the energy of a photon of frequency 5 × 10^14 Hz? (h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the radius of the third orbit is how many times the radius of the first orbit?
questions.explanation: Orbit radius is proportional to n^2, so r3/r1 = 3^2/1^2 = 9.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Pauli's exclusion principle and explain what it implies for the maximum number of electrons in one orbital.
questions.answer: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of all four quantum numbers, so an orbital can hold at most two electrons, which must have opposite spins.
keyPoints: No two electrons share identical n, l, ml and ms
Electrons in one orbital differ in spin quantum number
Maximum occupancy of an orbital is 2
questions.explanation: Two electrons in one orbital already share n, l and ml, so they must differ in ms (+1/2 and -1/2).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of radial nodes and angular nodes in a 3p orbital.
questions.explanation: For 3p, n = 3 and l = 1, so use n - l - 1 for radial nodes and l for angular nodes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to the modern periodic law, the properties of elements are a periodic function of their
questions.explanation: Moseley's work led to the modern periodic law, which is based on atomic number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the largest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group as more shells are added, and caesium is lowest among these in group 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among Na, Mg, Ne and O, which has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Neon has a stable, filled octet and a high effective nuclear charge, so removing an electron is hardest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among the halogens F, Cl, Br and I, which has the most negative electron gain enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is so small that electron-electron repulsion reduces its value, so chlorine has the most negative electron gain enthalpy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the isoelectronic species O2-, F-, Na+ and Mg2+ has the largest ionic radius?
questions.explanation: All have 10 electrons, but O2- has the fewest protons (8), so the weakest pull on the electrons and the largest radius.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An element has the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5. In which period and group does it lie?
questions.explanation: The outermost shell is n = 3, so period 3; it has 7 valence electrons, so it is in group 17 (a halogen).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The first ionisation enthalpy of boron is lower than that of beryllium mainly because
options: boron has a larger atomic radius than beryllium
the electron lost by boron comes from a 2p orbital, which is higher in energy and shielded by the 2s electrons
boron has a smaller nuclear charge than beryllium
questions.explanation: The 2p electron of boron is less penetrating and easier to remove than the 2s electron of beryllium, even though boron has the larger nuclear charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is a cation always smaller than its parent atom?
questions.answer: Loss of electrons reduces electron-electron repulsion and often removes a whole shell, while the nuclear charge stays the same, so the remaining electrons are pulled in more strongly.
keyPoints: Fewer electrons, same number of protons
Higher effective nuclear charge per electron
Often the outermost shell is lost
questions.explanation: With the same nuclear charge holding fewer electrons, the electron cloud contracts.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is the second ionisation enthalpy of sodium much larger than its first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.answer: After the first electron is removed Na+ has the stable neon configuration; the next electron must be taken from an inner, closer shell held by a higher effective nuclear charge.
keyPoints: Electron comes from an inner shell nearer the nucleus
Much greater energy needed than for the single 3s electron
questions.explanation: The first electron is a lone, well-shielded 3s electron, whereas the second is a tightly held 2p electron.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of a methane (CH4) molecule?
questions.explanation: Carbon in methane is sp3 hybridised with four bond pairs, giving a tetrahedral shape with 109.5 degree angles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which type of bond is present in sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, and the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions are held by electrostatic attraction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethene, C2H4?
questions.explanation: Each carbon forms three sigma bonds and one pi bond, which means sp2 hybridisation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to molecular orbital theory, what is the bond order of the O2 molecule?
questions.explanation: O2 has 10 bonding and 6 antibonding electrons, so bond order = (10 - 6)/2 = 2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules has a zero dipole moment?
questions.explanation: CO2 is linear, so the two equal C=O bond dipoles cancel each other.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of the XeF4 molecule?
questions.explanation: Xenon has four bond pairs and two lone pairs; the lone pairs sit opposite each other, giving a square planar molecule.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The bond angles in CH4, NH3 and H2O decrease in the order 109.5 degrees, 107 degrees and 104.5 degrees. This is best explained by the fact that
options: lone pairs repel bond pairs more strongly than bond pairs repel one another
carbon is sp3 hybridised while oxygen is sp hybridised
questions.explanation: The number of lone pairs increases from 0 to 1 to 2, and lone pair-bond pair repulsion squeezes the H-X-H angle.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define bond order and give its value for the nitrogen molecule N2.
questions.answer: Bond order is half the difference between the number of electrons in bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals; for N2 it is 3.
keyPoints: N2 has 10 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons
Bond order of N2 = 3, a triple bond
questions.explanation: A higher bond order means a shorter, stronger bond, which explains the very high stability of N2.

crossCheck.note: Bond order formula and value 3 are right, but the keyPoints say N2 has 10 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons. Correct counts are 8 bonding and 2 antibonding (bond order (8-2)/2 = 3). Reviewed: kept. NCERT counts all 14 electrons (Nb = 10, Na = 4); the checker used valence electrons only (8 and 2). Both give 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does water have a much higher boiling point than hydrogen sulphide although H2S has the larger molar mass?
questions.answer: Oxygen is highly electronegative and small, so water molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which need much more energy to break; H2S does not hydrogen-bond appreciably.
keyPoints: H2S has only weak dipole and van der Waals forces
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding outweighs the effect of larger mass on van der Waals forces.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its
questions.explanation: This is Boyle's law: P × V is constant at constant temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero, 0 K, corresponds to -273.15 °C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the pressure of 2 mol of an ideal gas in a 10 L vessel at 300 K? (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas mixture has 2 mol of N2 and 3 mol of O2 at a total pressure of 5 atm. What is the partial pressure of N2?
questions.explanation: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure = (2/5) × 5 = 2 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 2.0 L at 300 K and constant pressure. What volume will it occupy at 450 K?
questions.explanation: By Charles's law V2 = V1 × T2/T1 = 2.0 × 450/300 = 3.0 L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which gas effuses fastest under the same conditions?
questions.explanation: By Graham's law rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass, and H2 has the lowest molar mass.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas X diffuses at half the rate of methane (molar mass 16 g/mol) under the same conditions. What is the molar mass of X?
questions.explanation: rate(X)/rate(CH4) = sqrt(16/M) = 1/2, so 16/M = 1/4 and M = 64 g/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Real gases deviate strongly from ideal behaviour at very high pressure mainly because
options: the temperature of the gas always falls
the volume occupied by the molecules becomes comparable to the volume of the container
the molecules lose mass when compressed
questions.explanation: The ideal gas model assumes negligible molecular volume, which fails when the gas is compressed so much that molecular volume is a significant fraction of the total.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many moles of gas are present in 5.6 L of a gas at 273 K and 1 atm? (Molar volume at these conditions = 22.4 L/mol)
keyPoints: One mole occupies 22.4 L at 273 K and 1 atm
questions.explanation: Divide the given volume by the molar volume: 5.6/22.4 = 0.25.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an intensive property?
questions.explanation: Density does not depend on the amount of matter, whereas volume, mass and enthalpy do.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A system that exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings is called a(n)
questions.explanation: An isolated system cannot exchange matter or energy; a closed system can exchange energy only.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A system absorbs 100 J of heat and does 40 J of work on its surroundings. What is the change in internal energy (using the IUPAC sign convention)?
questions.explanation: ΔU = q + w = +100 J + (-40 J) = +60 J, since work done by the system is negative.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), the relation between ΔH and ΔU is
questions.explanation: ΔH = ΔU + Δng RT and Δng = 2 - 4 = -2, so ΔH = ΔU - 2RT.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Given C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔH = -394 kJ/mol and CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔH = -283 kJ/mol, what is the enthalpy change for C(s) + 1/2 O2(g) → CO(g)?
questions.explanation: By Hess's law, ΔH = -394 - (-283) = -111 kJ/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = +30 kJ/mol and ΔS = +100 J/(K mol). Above what temperature does it become spontaneous?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS < 0 when T > 30000 J / 100 J K^-1 = 300 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For which of the following processes is the entropy change of the system negative?
questions.explanation: Condensation makes the system more ordered, so entropy decreases, whereas the other three increase disorder.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The combustion of 1 mol of methane releases 890 kJ. How much heat is released by burning 8 g of methane? (CH4 = 16 g/mol)
questions.explanation: 8 g is 0.5 mol, so heat released = 0.5 × 890 = 445 kJ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why the enthalpy of neutralisation of any strong acid with a strong base is nearly constant at about -57 kJ per mole of water formed.
questions.answer: Strong acids and bases are completely ionised, so the only net reaction is H+ + OH- → H2O, which is the same for every pair.
keyPoints: Strong acids and bases dissociate completely
Spectator ions do not take part
Net change is H+(aq) + OH-(aq) → H2O(l)
questions.explanation: Since the net reaction is identical, the heat released per mole of water is nearly the same.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to Le Chatelier's principle, if the concentration of a reactant is increased at equilibrium, the equilibrium
options: shifts in the forward direction to use up the added reactant
questions.explanation: The system opposes the change by consuming some of the added reactant, forming more product.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the expression for Kc for the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g)?
questions.explanation: Kc is products raised to their coefficients divided by reactants raised to their coefficients.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of a 0.001 M solution of HCl at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid, so [H+] = 10^-3 M and pH = 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For which of the following reactions is Kp equal to Kc?
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc (RT)^Δng, and Δng = 0 only for H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) the equilibrium constant is 50 at a given temperature. What is the constant for 2HI(g) ⇌ H2(g) + I2(g) at that temperature?
questions.explanation: Reversing the reaction inverts K, so K = 1/50 = 0.02.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of a 0.01 M NaOH solution at 25 °C?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following is the solubility of AgCl lowest?
questions.explanation: The common ion Cl- in NaCl suppresses dissolution of AgCl, while NH3 even increases it by forming a complex.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following mixtures acts as an acidic buffer?
questions.explanation: A weak acid with its salt of a strong base resists pH change; HCl and HNO3 are strong acids, so they do not buffer.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For N2O4(g) ⇌ 2NO2(g), the equilibrium concentrations are [N2O4] = 0.2 M and [NO2] = 0.4 M. Calculate Kc.
questions.explanation: Substitute the equilibrium concentrations into the expression with NO2 squared.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in H2SO4?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is
questions.explanation: Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises the oxidation number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of chromium in K2Cr2O7?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu, the oxidising agent is
questions.explanation: Cu2+ gains electrons and is reduced, so it is the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a disproportionation reaction?
questions.explanation: In H2O2 oxygen (-1) is both oxidised to O2 (0) and reduced to H2O (-2).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In MnO4- + 5Fe2+ + 8H+ → Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O, how many electrons does each MnO4- ion gain?
questions.explanation: Mn changes from +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the average oxidation number of sulphur in the tetrathionate ion in Na2S4O6?
questions.explanation: 2(+1) + 4x + 6(-2) = 0 gives 4x = 10, so x = +2.5 on average.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does fluorine show only the -1 oxidation state and never a positive one in compounds?
questions.answer: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and has no d orbitals, so it always attracts the shared electrons and cannot lose electrons or expand its octet.
keyPoints: No vacant d orbitals to expand octet
questions.explanation: With every bond to a less electronegative element, fluorine takes the electrons and so is always -1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why hydrogen peroxide can act as both an oxidising agent and a reducing agent.
questions.answer: Oxygen in H2O2 has oxidation number -1, which lies between 0 (in O2) and -2 (in H2O), so it can be raised or lowered.
keyPoints: Oxidation number of O in H2O2 is -1
Can be reduced to water or hydroxide (-2)
questions.explanation: An element in an intermediate oxidation state can both increase and decrease it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which isotope of hydrogen is radioactive?
questions.explanation: Tritium (3H) is radioactive and emits beta particles, whereas protium and deuterium are stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of heavy water?
questions.explanation: Heavy water is deuterium oxide, D2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal imparts a golden-yellow colour to a Bunsen flame?
questions.explanation: Sodium gives an intense golden-yellow flame, lithium crimson red and potassium lilac.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na2CO3·10H2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Beryllium chloride is largely covalent while barium chloride is ionic. The best explanation is that
options: Be2+ is very small with high charge density, so it strongly polarises the chloride ion
beryllium has a lower ionisation enthalpy than barium
chlorine is less electronegative towards beryllium
questions.explanation: By Fajans' rules, a small, highly charged cation such as Be2+ distorts the anion's electron cloud and gives covalent character.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Give two reasons why hydrogen is placed separately from the alkali metals in some versions of the periodic table.
questions.answer: Hydrogen is a non-metal that exists as a diatomic gas, and it can also gain one electron to form H-, unlike alkali metals.
keyPoints: Forms H- ions by gaining an electron
Much higher ionisation enthalpy than alkali metals
questions.explanation: Hydrogen resembles both group 1 (one valence electron) and group 17 (needs one electron), so it fits neither group exactly.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is temporary hardness of water, what causes it, and how can it be removed?
questions.answer: Temporary hardness is due to dissolved bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium and is removed by boiling, which precipitates the carbonates.
keyPoints: Boiling decomposes them to insoluble carbonates
Can also be removed by Clark's method
questions.explanation: On heating, Ca(HCO3)2 → CaCO3 + H2O + CO2, so the calcium leaves the solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the reaction of sodium with water and explain why sodium is stored under kerosene.
questions.answer: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2. Sodium reacts vigorously with moisture and oxygen in air, so it is kept under kerosene.
keyPoints: Kerosene keeps out air and moisture
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and would otherwise catch fire or corrode in air.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct formula of borax?
questions.explanation: Borax is sodium tetraborate decahydrate, Na2B4O7·10H2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an allotrope of carbon?
questions.explanation: Fullerenes such as C60 are allotropes of carbon, as are diamond and graphite; the others are compounds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of each carbon atom in diamond?
questions.explanation: Each carbon is bonded to four others in a tetrahedral network, which means sp3 hybridisation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Anhydrous aluminium chloride exists as the dimer Al2Cl6 in the vapour state because
options: aluminium is electron-deficient and completes its octet by using lone pairs of bridging chlorine atoms
the dimer has ionic Al-Al bonds
questions.explanation: In AlCl3 aluminium has only six electrons; two molecules join through chlorine bridges that donate lone pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not because in graphite
options: all four electrons of carbon are held in sigma bonds
each carbon uses three electrons in sigma bonds and the fourth is delocalised between the layers
questions.explanation: Graphite has sp2 carbon in layers, and the leftover p electrons are delocalised and free to move along the layers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide poisonous to humans?
questions.answer: CO binds to the iron in haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen does, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and blocking oxygen transport.
keyPoints: Oxygen carrying capacity of blood falls
questions.explanation: The body's tissues become starved of oxygen, causing headache, unconsciousness and possibly death.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the inert pair effect? Give one example from group 14.
questions.answer: It is the reluctance of the two outer s electrons to take part in bonding in heavier p-block elements, so a lower oxidation state is more stable; for example Pb2+ is more stable than Pb4+.
keyPoints: ns2 electrons stay unused in heavier elements
Lower oxidation state becomes more stable
Example: Pb(II) more stable than Pb(IV)
questions.explanation: Poor shielding by d and f electrons makes the s electrons held tightly, so they are not lost easily.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Boric acid is a weak monobasic Lewis acid. Write the equation showing how it behaves in water.
keyPoints: Boron accepts a hydroxide ion from water (Lewis acid)
questions.explanation: It does not donate H+ itself; it accepts OH- from water, which leaves H3O+ in solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CH2CH2OH?
questions.explanation: A three-carbon chain with an -OH on the first carbon is propan-1-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The functional group present in a ketone is
options: a carbonyl group joined to two carbon atoms
questions.explanation: A ketone has a C=O group bonded to two carbon atoms, unlike an aldehyde where one is hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among alkyl carbocations, which is the most stable?
questions.explanation: A tertiary carbocation is stabilised by three alkyl groups through the inductive effect and hyperconjugation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many sigma and pi bonds are present in propene, CH2=CH-CH3?
questions.explanation: There are 6 C-H sigma bonds, 2 C-C sigma bonds (one in C=C) = 8 sigma, and one pi bond in the double bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing chlorine (-I effect) stabilises the carboxylate ion, whereas alkyl groups destabilise it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between homolytic and heterolytic bond fission.
questions.answer: In homolytic fission the shared pair is split equally, one electron to each atom, forming free radicals; in heterolytic fission one atom takes both electrons, forming a cation and an anion.
keyPoints: Homolytic: one electron to each fragment, gives free radicals
Heterolytic: both electrons go to one atom, gives ions
questions.explanation: The type of fission determines whether the reaction proceeds through radicals or ionic intermediates.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the structural formulae of the two chain isomers of C4H10 and name them.
questions.explanation: They are chain isomers because they differ in the arrangement of the carbon skeleton.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a nucleophile? Give two examples.
questions.answer: A nucleophile is an electron-rich species that donates a pair of electrons to an electron-deficient centre, for example OH- and NH3 (also CN-).
questions.explanation: Nucleophile means nucleus-loving; it seeks a positively charged or partially positive atom.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkene series?
questions.explanation: Alkenes with one double bond have the general formula CnH2n.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent is used as a simple test for unsaturation in a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise the orange-brown bromine water by addition across the double or triple bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product when HBr adds to propene in the absence of peroxide?
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule hydrogen goes to the carbon with more hydrogens, so bromine attaches to the middle carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzene most characteristically undergoes
questions.explanation: The delocalised pi electron cloud attracts electrophiles, and substitution keeps the aromatic ring intact.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is aromatic according to Hückel's (4n + 2) pi electron rule?
questions.explanation: Benzene is planar, cyclic and fully conjugated with 6 pi electrons (n = 1); cyclobutadiene has 4 and cyclooctatetraene has 8.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation of the Wurtz reaction for the preparation of ethane from bromomethane.
keyPoints: Alkyl halide treated with sodium metal
Two alkyl groups join to give a higher alkane
questions.explanation: Sodium removes the halogen and the two methyl groups couple to form a C-C bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why benzene is more stable than the hypothetical 'cyclohexatriene' with three fixed double bonds.
questions.answer: Benzene's pi electrons are delocalised over all six carbons (resonance), which lowers its energy; its resonance energy is about 150 kJ/mol and all C-C bonds are equal in length.
keyPoints: All C-C bonds equal, intermediate length
questions.explanation: The measured heat of hydrogenation of benzene is much lower than three times that of cyclohexene, showing extra stability.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is a terminal alkyne such as ethyne more acidic than ethene or ethane?
questions.answer: The sp-hybridised carbon has 50% s-character and is more electronegative, so the C-H bond is more polarised and the acetylide ion is more stable.
keyPoints: More electronegative carbon holds the lone pair better
Terminal H can be removed by strong bases like NaNH2
questions.explanation: Greater s-character stabilises the negative charge on carbon in the conjugate base.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The law of conservation of mass was put forward by
questions.explanation: Lavoisier showed that in a chemical reaction the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which law states that a pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in the same proportion by mass?
questions.explanation: This is the law of definite (constant) proportions, given by Proust.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many molecules are present in 4.4 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16; NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 50 mL of 2 M HCl is diluted with water to a final volume of 100 mL. What is the new molarity?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A hydrocarbon has the empirical formula CH and a molar mass of 78 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (C = 12, H = 1)
questions.explanation: The empirical formula mass is 13, and 78/13 = 6, so the molecular formula is C6H6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethene burns as C2H4 + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O. What mass of oxygen is needed to burn 2.8 g of ethene completely? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.explanation: 2.8 g of C2H4 (28 g/mol) is 0.1 mol, which needs 0.3 mol O2 = 0.3 × 32 = 9.6 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is meant by a limiting reagent in a chemical reaction?
questions.answer: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first and therefore decides the maximum amount of product formed.
keyPoints: It limits the amount of product
questions.explanation: Once the limiting reagent is exhausted, the reaction stops even if other reactants remain.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 6 g of hydrogen react with excess nitrogen according to N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3. Calculate the mass of ammonia formed. (N = 14, H = 1)
questions.explanation: The mole ratio H2 : NH3 is 3 : 2, so 3 mol of H2 yields 2 mol of NH3 weighing 34 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but different numbers of neutrons, and so different mass numbers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cathode rays are streams of
questions.explanation: Thomson's experiments with discharge tubes showed that cathode rays consist of negatively charged electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are present in a nitrogen atom (Z = 7) in its ground state?
questions.explanation: The configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3 has three 2p electrons occupying separate orbitals with parallel spins (Hund's rule).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to the Aufbau principle, after the 3p orbitals are filled, the next orbital to be filled is
questions.explanation: The 4s orbital has lower energy than 3d (lower n + l value, or n + l equal and lower n), so it fills first.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass m moving with velocity v is
questions.explanation: de Broglie related wavelength to momentum by λ = h/(mv).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle implies that
options: electrons move in fixed circular orbits
the exact position and the exact momentum of an electron cannot both be known simultaneously
questions.explanation: The product of the uncertainties in position and momentum is at least h/4π, which rules out sharply defined electron orbits.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at 1.0 × 10^6 m/s. (m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s)
questions.explanation: Substituting gives 6.626 × 10^-34 / 9.1 × 10^-25 = 7.28 × 10^-10 m, comparable to atomic dimensions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity and illustrate it with the 2p electrons of nitrogen.
questions.answer: Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly with parallel spins before any orbital gets a second electron; in nitrogen the three 2p electrons occupy 2px, 2py and 2pz separately.
keyPoints: Degenerate orbitals are filled singly first
Singly occupied electrons have parallel spins
questions.explanation: Keeping electrons apart reduces repulsion and gives a lower energy, more stable arrangement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the modern long form of the periodic table, the noble gases are placed in
questions.explanation: The noble gases form group 18, with complete outer shells.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The transition elements belong to which block of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: In transition elements the last electron enters a d subshell, so they form the d-block.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale (about 4.0).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of elements shows a diagonal relationship?
questions.explanation: Lithium (group 1, period 2) resembles magnesium (group 2, period 3) in several properties because of similar charge/size ratios.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An element X has the electronic configuration [Ne] 3s2 3p4. Which statement about X is correct?
options: It is a metal belonging to group 14
It is a non-metal that forms a basic oxide
It forms an acidic oxide and its common simple ion is X2-
questions.explanation: Six valence electrons put X in group 16 (sulphur); non-metal oxides such as SO2 are acidic, and X gains 2 electrons to form X2-.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the elements Be, B, C and N has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Across period 2 the ionisation enthalpy generally rises with increasing nuclear charge, and nitrogen also has a stable half-filled 2p subshell.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do the elements of a group show similar chemical properties?
questions.answer: All elements in a group have the same number of electrons in the outermost shell, and chemical behaviour is decided by valence electrons.
keyPoints: Properties change gradually with increasing size
questions.explanation: For example, all alkali metals have ns1 configuration and form +1 ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Arrange Na, Mg, Al and Si in increasing order of metallic character and give the reason.
questions.answer: Si < Al < Mg < Na. Metallic character decreases across a period as ionisation enthalpy increases and the tendency to lose electrons falls.
keyPoints: Ionisation enthalpy rises across the period
Less tendency to lose electrons going left to right
questions.explanation: Sodium loses its single outer electron most readily, so it is the most metallic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following species is a coordinate (dative) covalent bond present?
questions.explanation: In NH4+ the lone pair on nitrogen is donated to H+, forming a coordinate bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ionic compounds generally have high melting points mainly because of
options: weak van der Waals forces between molecules
strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions in the lattice
the presence of discrete covalent molecules
questions.explanation: A great deal of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic forces holding ions in the crystal lattice.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many lone pairs of electrons are present on the oxygen atom in a water molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has six valence electrons; two are used in O-H bonds, and the remaining four form two lone pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of phosphorus in PCl5?
questions.explanation: Five bond pairs around P need five hybrid orbitals, which is sp3d with a trigonal bipyramidal shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which sequence shows the carbon-carbon bond lengths in increasing order?
questions.explanation: A higher bond order draws the nuclei closer, so the triple bond is shortest and the single bond is longest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does the He2 molecule not exist under normal conditions?
options: Its bond order is zero because bonding and antibonding orbitals are both filled
Helium atoms are too heavy to combine
questions.explanation: Four electrons fill the σ1s and σ*1s orbitals, so bond order = (2 - 2)/2 = 0 and there is no net bonding.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Draw (describe) the Lewis structure of carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: O=C=O: carbon in the centre is doubly bonded to each oxygen, and each oxygen carries two lone pairs.
keyPoints: Carbon double bonded to each oxygen
Each oxygen has two lone pairs
questions.explanation: Total valence electrons are 4 + 6 + 6 = 16, shared as two double bonds and four lone pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: NF3 has a much smaller dipole moment than NH3 even though fluorine is more electronegative than hydrogen. Explain.
questions.answer: In NH3 the bond dipoles point toward nitrogen, in the same direction as the lone-pair dipole, so they add; in NF3 the bond dipoles point toward fluorine, opposite to the lone-pair dipole, so they partly cancel.
keyPoints: NH3: N-H bond dipoles and lone-pair dipole reinforce
NF3: N-F bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair dipole
Net dipole moment is therefore smaller in NF3
questions.explanation: The direction of the bond dipoles relative to the lone pair determines the net dipole, not just the electronegativity difference.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which type of intermolecular force is present in all molecules, including non-polar ones?
questions.explanation: Temporary induced dipoles give dispersion forces in every molecule; the other forces need ions or permanent dipoles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure becomes equal to
questions.explanation: Boiling starts when vapour bubbles can form against the external pressure, so vapour pressure equals external pressure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On heating a liquid, its viscosity generally
questions.explanation: Molecules gain kinetic energy and overcome intermolecular forces more easily, so the liquid flows more readily.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 10 L of hydrogen and 10 L of methane at the same temperature and pressure contain
questions.explanation: By Avogadro's law equal volumes of gases at the same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of the compressibility factor Z for an ideal gas?
questions.explanation: Z = PV/nRT, which equals 1 at all pressures for an ideal gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the density of carbon dioxide at 273 K and 1 atm? (Molar mass 44 g/mol; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: Density = molar mass / molar volume = 44/22.4 = 1.96 g/L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: When a gas in a rigid container is heated, its pressure rises because
options: the molecules move faster and hit the walls more often and with greater force
questions.explanation: According to kinetic theory, pressure comes from molecular collisions with the wall, and a higher temperature means a higher average kinetic energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the critical temperature of a gas?
questions.answer: It is the temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied however high the pressure applied.
keyPoints: Highest temperature at which liquefaction is possible
Above it only the gaseous state exists
Critical pressure is the pressure needed at that temperature
questions.explanation: Above the critical temperature the kinetic energy of molecules is too high for attractions to hold them as a liquid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 0.5 g of a gas occupies 0.25 L at 300 K and 2 atm. Calculate its molar mass. (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)
questions.explanation: Using M = wRT/PV gives 0.5 × 24.63 / 0.5 = 24.6 g/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The heat exchanged by a system at constant pressure is equal to the change in its
questions.explanation: By definition, qp = ΔH for a process at constant pressure when only pressure-volume work is possible.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy of formation of O2(g) in its standard state?
questions.explanation: By convention the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its most stable form is zero.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a state function?
options: Heat absorbed in a given path
questions.explanation: Internal energy depends only on the state of the system, whereas heat and work depend on the path.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At equilibrium the Gibbs energy change ΔG of a reaction is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium there is no net driving force, so ΔG = 0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Bond enthalpies are H-H 436, Cl-Cl 243 and H-Cl 431 kJ/mol. What is ΔH for H2(g) + Cl2(g) → 2HCl(g)?
questions.explanation: ΔH = bonds broken - bonds formed = (436 + 243) - 2(431) = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 100 g of water from 25 °C to 35 °C? (specific heat of water = 4.18 J g^-1 K^-1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gas expands freely into a vacuum in an insulated container. Which statement is correct?
options: Work done is zero and the temperature stays constant
The temperature of the gas rises
questions.explanation: With no external pressure w = 0, and with no heat exchange q = 0, so ΔU = 0; for an ideal gas this means the temperature is unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between an exothermic and an endothermic reaction with the sign of ΔH and one example of each.
questions.answer: An exothermic reaction releases heat and has negative ΔH, for example combustion of methane; an endothermic reaction absorbs heat and has positive ΔH, for example decomposition of calcium carbonate.
questions.explanation: The sign of ΔH tells whether the products have lower or higher enthalpy than the reactants.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ice melts at 273 K with an enthalpy of fusion of 6.01 kJ/mol. Calculate the entropy change for melting 1 mol of ice.
keyPoints: At the melting point ΔG = 0, so ΔS = ΔH/T
questions.explanation: At the equilibrium temperature of a phase change, TΔS equals ΔH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The numerical value of the equilibrium constant of a reaction depends on
questions.explanation: For a given reaction K changes only with temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A catalyst added to a reaction at equilibrium
options: shifts the equilibrium to the right
shifts the equilibrium to the left
speeds up forward and backward reactions equally without changing Kc
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both directions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but not changed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the conjugate base of the hydrogen sulphate ion, HSO4-?
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed by removing a proton, and HSO4- minus H+ gives SO4 2-.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hydroxide ion concentration of a solution with pH = 9 at 25 °C?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: BF3 has an incomplete octet and accepts an electron pair; NH3, H2O and OH- donate pairs.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, increasing the pressure at constant temperature shifts the equilibrium
options: nowhere, since pressure has no effect
to the right, because there are fewer moles of gas on the right
to the right, because the reaction is endothermic
questions.explanation: Four moles of gas become two, so by Le Chatelier's principle higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The solubility product Ksp of AgCl is 1.8 × 10^-10 at 25 °C. What is its molar solubility in pure water?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is an aqueous solution of sodium acetate basic?
questions.answer: The acetate ion is the conjugate base of a weak acid and reacts with water: CH3COO- + H2O ⇌ CH3COOH + OH-, producing excess OH- ions.
keyPoints: Salt of weak acid and strong base
questions.explanation: Because [OH-] exceeds [H+], the solution has pH above 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the pH of 0.1 M acetic acid solution. (Ka = 1.8 × 10^-5; assume the dissociation is small)
questions.explanation: For a weak acid, [H+] = sqrt(Ka C) when dissociation is much less than the total concentration.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reducing agent is a substance that
options: loses electrons and is itself oxidised
gains electrons and is itself reduced
decreases the oxidation number of itself
questions.explanation: A reducing agent donates electrons to another species, so its own oxidation number increases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in hydrogen peroxide, H2O2?
questions.explanation: With each H at +1, the two oxygen atoms share -2, so each is -1 (a peroxide).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of chlorine in HClO4?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the average oxidation state of iron in Fe3O4?
questions.explanation: 3x + 4(-2) = 0 gives x = +8/3; it is a mixed oxide of one Fe2+ and two Fe3+.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which metal will displace copper from a copper sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc is above copper in the activity series and so reduces Cu2+ to copper metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In a galvanic cell, oxidation takes place at the
questions.explanation: The anode is by definition the electrode where oxidation occurs, releasing electrons to the external circuit.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many electrons does one dichromate ion Cr2O7 2- gain when it is reduced to two Cr3+ ions in acidic solution?
questions.explanation: Each chromium changes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons, so two chromium atoms gain 6 electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2Na + Cl2 → 2NaCl, identify the oxidising agent and the reducing agent.
questions.answer: Sodium is the reducing agent (it loses electrons, 0 to +1) and chlorine is the oxidising agent (it gains electrons, 0 to -1).
keyPoints: Na oxidised from 0 to +1: reducing agent
Cl2 reduced from 0 to -1: oxidising agent
Electrons move from Na to Cl
questions.explanation: The species that is oxidised acts as the reducing agent, and the species reduced is the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the oxidation number of oxygen in OF2 and explain why it is not -2.
questions.answer: +2. Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen, so fluorine is -1 and the oxygen balances with +2.
keyPoints: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxygen shows -2 only when bonded to elements less electronegative than itself.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In sodium hydride, NaH, hydrogen is present as
questions.explanation: NaH is an ionic hydride made of Na+ and H- ions, since hydrogen gains an electron from the metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of quicklime?
questions.explanation: Quicklime is calcium oxide, CaO, made by heating limestone.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, obtained by heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) at about 393 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The reactivity of alkali metals towards water increases in the order
questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down the group as ionisation enthalpy decreases, so lithium reacts slowly and caesium explosively.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hard water does not give a good lather with soap because
options: Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions react with soap to form an insoluble scum
it has a low boiling point
questions.explanation: Soap (sodium stearate and similar salts) forms insoluble calcium and magnesium salts, which separate as scum.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which method is used for the laboratory preparation of dihydrogen?
options: Granulated zinc with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2; copper is less reactive than hydrogen and does not react with dilute HCl.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Unlike the carbonates of the other alkali metals, lithium carbonate
options: decomposes on heating to give Li2O and CO2
questions.explanation: The small Li+ ion polarises the carbonate ion strongly, so Li2CO3 decomposes on heating while other alkali carbonates are stable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do alkaline earth metals have higher melting points than alkali metals of the same period?
questions.answer: Each alkaline earth atom contributes two valence electrons and forms a smaller 2+ ion, so metallic bonding is stronger than in the alkali metals, which contribute one electron.
keyPoints: Smaller atoms and higher nuclear charge
questions.explanation: Stronger metallic bonds need more energy to break, so melting points are higher.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why ice floats on water.
questions.answer: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold water molecules in an open cage-like structure with empty spaces, so ice has a lower density than liquid water.
keyPoints: Each water molecule is hydrogen-bonded to four others in ice
questions.explanation: When ice melts the open structure partly collapses, so liquid water is denser.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust?
questions.explanation: Aluminium makes up about 8% of the Earth's crust by mass, more than any other metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Quartz is a crystalline form of
questions.explanation: Quartz is crystalline silica, SiO2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Dry ice is
questions.explanation: Dry ice is solid CO2, which sublimes directly into gas at about -78 °C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Silicones are polymers whose backbone consists of repeating units of
questions.explanation: Silicones have an alternating silicon-oxygen chain with organic groups attached to silicon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which compound is commonly called inorganic benzene?
questions.explanation: Borazine, B3N3H6, has a planar six-membered ring of alternating B and N atoms, similar to benzene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many three-centre two-electron (banana) bonds are present in diborane, B2H6?
questions.explanation: Two bridging hydrogens each link the two boron atoms through a three-centre two-electron bond; the four terminal B-H bonds are ordinary.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: CCl4 is not hydrolysed by water, whereas SiCl4 is hydrolysed readily. This is because
options: silicon has vacant 3d orbitals that can accept a lone pair from water, but carbon has no d orbitals
carbon is more electronegative than silicon and attracts water
silicon forms stronger bonds with chlorine than carbon does
questions.explanation: Silicon can expand its coordination number using 3d orbitals, so water can attack it; carbon, having no d orbitals in its second shell, cannot.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation showing that aluminium reacts with sodium hydroxide solution, and state the property it demonstrates.
questions.answer: 2Al + 2NaOH + 6H2O → 2Na[Al(OH)4] + 3H2. Aluminium is amphoteric, as it also reacts with acids.
keyPoints: Aluminium reacts with both acids and bases: amphoteric
questions.explanation: Reacting with both acids and strong alkalis shows amphoteric behaviour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why does carbon show catenation to a much greater extent than other group 14 elements?
questions.answer: The C-C bond is very strong because of small size of carbon, and carbon forms stable bonds with itself, whereas bond enthalpies decrease down the group.
keyPoints: Small size gives strong C-C bonds
Bond enthalpy decreases from C to Pb
questions.explanation: The high C-C bond enthalpy (about 348 kJ/mol) makes long stable chains possible.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different
questions.explanation: Isomers share a molecular formula but differ in the structural or spatial arrangement of atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by
questions.explanation: Each member differs from the next by one -CH2- unit.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many carbon atoms are present in the compound 2,2-dimethylbutane?
questions.explanation: The parent chain butane has 4 carbons, and the two methyl groups add 2 more, giving 6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons, and the methyl is on carbon 2 when numbered from the nearer end.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an electrophile?
questions.explanation: NO2+ is electron-deficient and accepts an electron pair; the others have lone pairs and act as nucleophiles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many hyperconjugation structures can be written for the ethyl carbocation, CH3CH2+?
questions.explanation: Hyperconjugation involves the C-H bonds on the carbon next to the positive centre, and the CH3 group has three such bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following groups shows a +M (positive mesomeric) effect?
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group has a lone pair on nitrogen that can be donated into the pi system; the other groups withdraw electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What type of isomerism is shown by butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol?
questions.answer: Position isomerism, because the -OH group is on different carbon atoms of the same carbon chain.
keyPoints: Different position of the functional group
questions.explanation: Both are C4H10O and have a four-carbon chain, but -OH is on carbon 1 in one and carbon 2 in the other.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Describe how nitrogen in an organic compound is detected by Lassaigne's test.
questions.answer: The compound is fused with sodium to give sodium cyanide; the extract is boiled with iron(II) sulphate and acidified, and Prussian blue colour shows nitrogen.
keyPoints: Add FeSO4 and then acidify with dilute acid
questions.explanation: Covalent nitrogen is converted into the ionic cyanide, which is then detected as the iron complex.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the simplest alkane?
questions.explanation: Methane, CH4, has one carbon atom and is the first member of the alkane series.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Alkenes can show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism because of
options: restricted rotation about the C=C double bond
free rotation about C-C single bonds
questions.explanation: The pi bond prevents rotation around the double bond, so different spatial arrangements of groups are fixed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: When ethyne is passed through a red-hot iron tube at about 873 K, the product is
questions.explanation: Three molecules of ethyne polymerise (cyclic trimerisation) to give benzene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Partial hydrogenation of but-2-yne using Lindlar's catalyst gives mainly
questions.explanation: Lindlar's catalyst (poisoned palladium) adds hydrogen to the same face of the triple bond and stops at the alkene, giving the cis isomer.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the presence of a peroxide, HBr adds to propene to give mainly
questions.explanation: The peroxide effect (Kharasch) causes anti-Markovnikov addition via a free radical mechanism, putting bromine on the terminal carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent combination is used for the nitration of benzene?
questions.explanation: The mixture generates the nitronium ion, NO2+, which is the attacking electrophile.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Reductive ozonolysis of but-2-ene gives
questions.explanation: The double bond between C2 and C3 is cleaved, so each CH3-CH= half becomes CH3CHO.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane.
keyPoints: Products are carbon dioxide and water
questions.explanation: Carbon balance gives 3 CO2, hydrogen balance gives 4 H2O, and oxygen then totals 10 atoms, so 5 O2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why the -OH group on benzene directs an incoming electrophile to the ortho and para positions while the -NO2 group directs to the meta position.
questions.answer: -OH donates electron density to the ring by resonance (+M), increasing it at ortho and para positions; -NO2 withdraws electrons (-M, -I), lowering density mostly at ortho and para, so meta is least deactivated.
keyPoints: Electron density pattern decides the position of attack
questions.explanation: Electrophiles attack the position of highest electron density, which differs for donor and acceptor substituents.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a uniform mixture of several gases, so it is a homogeneous mixture; the other options are pure substances.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the molar mass of sulphuric acid, H2SO4? (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many atoms are present in 0.5 mol of oxygen gas, O2? (NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol of O2 is 0.5 × 6.022 × 10^23 molecules, and each molecule has 2 atoms, giving 6.022 × 10^23 atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the mass of nitrogen gas in 11.2 L at 273 K and 1 atm? (N = 14; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: 11.2 L is 0.5 mol of N2, and 0.5 × 28 g/mol = 14 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following contains the largest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: NH3 has 4 atoms per molecule, CO2 and H2O have 3, and O2 has 2, so 1 mol of NH3 has the most atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of water of crystallisation in CuSO4·5H2O? (Cu = 63.5, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What volume of 0.5 M NaOH solution contains 2 g of NaOH? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: 2 g is 0.05 mol, and volume = 0.05 mol / 0.5 mol per L = 0.1 L = 100 mL.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State the law of multiple proportions and illustrate it with carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide.
questions.answer: When two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a simple whole-number ratio. In CO and CO2, 12 g of carbon combines with 16 g and 32 g of oxygen, a ratio of 1 : 2.
keyPoints: Fixed mass of one element, varying mass of the other
CO and CO2: 16 g and 32 g of oxygen per 12 g carbon, ratio 1:2
questions.explanation: This law was proposed by Dalton and supports the atomic theory.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calcium carbonate decomposes as CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. What mass of CaCO3 must be heated to obtain 11.2 L of CO2 at 273 K and 1 atm? (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: The mole ratio CaCO3 : CO2 is 1 : 1, so 0.5 mol of CaCO3 (50 g) is needed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many electrons are present in a magnesium ion, Mg2+? (Atomic number of Mg = 12)
questions.explanation: A neutral Mg atom has 12 electrons; Mg2+ has lost 2, so it has 10.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following particles has the smallest mass?
questions.explanation: An electron has a mass of about 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, nearly 1/1836 of a proton.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of the azimuthal quantum number l for a p orbital?
questions.explanation: s, p, d and f orbitals have l = 0, 1, 2 and 3 respectively.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many orbitals are there in a d subshell?
questions.explanation: For l = 2 the magnetic quantum number takes 2l + 1 = 5 values.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In order of decreasing wavelength: radio waves, microwaves, visible light, X-rays, so X-rays are shortest here.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The energy of an electron in the nth orbit of hydrogen is -2.18 × 10^-18/n^2 J. What is its energy in the n = 2 orbit?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is paramagnetic?
questions.explanation: Fe3+ is 3d5 with five unpaired electrons; Zn2+ and Cu+ are 3d10 and Sc3+ is 3d0, so all of those are diamagnetic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the ground state electronic configuration of copper (Z = 29) and explain why it is not [Ar] 3d9 4s2.
questions.answer: [Ar] 3d10 4s1. A completely filled d subshell is extra stable, so one 4s electron moves into the 3d subshell.
keyPoints: Fully filled d10 gives extra stability
Exchange energy and symmetry favour this arrangement
questions.explanation: Cu and Cr are the common exceptions to the simple filling order for this reason.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the wavelength of light emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 3 to n = 2. (R_H = 1.097 × 10^7 m^-1)
questions.answer: About 6.56 × 10^-7 m (656 nm), in the visible region
questions.explanation: This is the first line (H-alpha) of the Balmer series.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which scientist arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's table left gaps for elements such as gallium and germanium and predicted their properties.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: All the elements in the same period of the periodic table have the same number of
questions.explanation: The period number equals the number of occupied electron shells.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Elements with atomic numbers 3, 11 and 19 are
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium all have one valence electron and are group 1 alkali metals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius?
questions.explanation: These ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons), and Al3+ has the highest nuclear charge, which pulls the electrons in most.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: Al2O3 reacts with both acids and bases; Na2O and MgO are basic and SO2 is acidic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The atomic radii quoted for noble gases are unusually large compared with the elements next to them in the same period because
options: they are van der Waals radii, which are larger than covalent radii
they have more electron shells than the neighbouring elements
they have a lower nuclear charge
they have no electrons in the outermost shell
questions.explanation: Noble gases form no covalent bonds, so only van der Waals radii can be measured, and these are larger than covalent radii.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The first ionisation enthalpy of oxygen is lower than that of nitrogen mainly because
options: in oxygen one 2p orbital holds a pair of electrons, and the repulsion makes that electron easier to remove
oxygen has a larger atomic radius than nitrogen
oxygen has a lower nuclear charge than nitrogen
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration, whereas in oxygen (2p4) the paired electrons repel each other.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Mendeleev's periodic law and mention one achievement of his periodic table.
questions.answer: The properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic masses. He left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties (for example eka-aluminium, later found as gallium).
keyPoints: Predictions later confirmed, such as gallium
questions.explanation: The modern law replaced atomic mass with atomic number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why do noble gases have positive electron gain enthalpy values?
questions.answer: Their valence shells are completely filled and stable, so an added electron must go into the next higher shell, which needs energy to be supplied.
keyPoints: Extra electron enters a new, higher energy shell
Energy has to be supplied, so the value is positive
questions.explanation: There is no net attraction from the nucleus for an additional electron in a new shell.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to the octet rule, atoms tend to have how many electrons in their outermost shell?
questions.explanation: Atoms combine to reach a stable noble gas configuration, commonly eight outer electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A covalent bond is formed by
options: complete transfer of electrons from one atom to another
sharing of electron pairs between two atoms
attraction between a metal and delocalised electrons only
questions.explanation: In a covalent bond two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of a water molecule?
questions.explanation: Oxygen has two bond pairs and two lone pairs, and the lone pairs make the molecule bent with a bond angle of about 104.5 degrees.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of boron trifluoride, BF3?
questions.explanation: Boron has three bond pairs and no lone pair, so BF3 is sp2 hybridised and planar with 120 degree angles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is linear?
questions.explanation: BeCl2 has two bond pairs and no lone pairs on Be (sp hybridisation), so it is linear.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many sigma and pi bonds are there in ethyne, HC≡CH?
questions.explanation: Two C-H sigma bonds and one C-C sigma bond make 3 sigma; the triple bond also has 2 pi bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among O2, O2-, O2 2- and O2+, which species has the shortest bond length?
questions.explanation: Bond orders are O2+ 2.5, O2 2, O2- 1.5 and O2 2- 1, and the highest bond order gives the shortest bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain sp3 hybridisation using methane as an example.
questions.answer: One 2s and three 2p orbitals of carbon mix to give four equivalent sp3 hybrid orbitals directed to the corners of a tetrahedron; each overlaps with a hydrogen 1s orbital to form four C-H sigma bonds.
keyPoints: One s and three p orbitals mix
Four equivalent sp3 orbitals, 109.5 degrees apart
Overlap with hydrogen 1s gives four sigma bonds
questions.explanation: Hybridisation explains why all four C-H bonds in methane are identical.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: o-Nitrophenol is steam volatile whereas p-nitrophenol is not. Explain.
questions.answer: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so its molecules do not associate and it is more volatile; p-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which gives association and lower volatility.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular bonding raises the boiling point, so only the ortho isomer distils with steam.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: A liquid takes the shape of its container but does not change its volume.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the SI unit of surface tension?
questions.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its SI unit is newton per metre.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The vapour pressure of a liquid increases with
options: increase in surface area of the liquid
increase in volume of the container
questions.explanation: A higher temperature gives more molecules enough energy to escape, raising vapour pressure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to the kinetic molecular theory, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy is (3/2)kT per molecule, so it depends on absolute temperature only.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 1.0 L at 27 °C and constant pressure. What is its volume at 127 °C?
questions.explanation: Convert to kelvin: V2 = 1.0 × 400/300 = 1.33 L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A vessel contains 2 g of hydrogen and 32 g of oxygen at a total pressure of 3 atm. What is the partial pressure of hydrogen? (H2 = 2 g/mol, O2 = 32 g/mol)
questions.explanation: There is 1 mol of each gas, so the mole fraction of H2 is 0.5 and its partial pressure is 0.5 × 3 = 1.5 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Dalton's law of partial pressures.
questions.answer: The total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases is the sum of the partial pressures that each gas would exert if it alone occupied the same volume at the same temperature.
keyPoints: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure
questions.explanation: Each gas behaves independently of the others in an ideal mixture.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Name two assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory that are not true for real gases.
questions.answer: The theory assumes that the volume of the gas molecules is negligible and that there are no attractive forces between them; in real gases both exist, especially at high pressure and low temperature.
keyPoints: Deviations are greatest at high pressure and low temperature
questions.explanation: The van der Waals equation corrects the ideal gas law for both effects.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explanation: The joule is the SI unit of energy, work and heat.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In an adiabatic process
options: no heat is exchanged between the system and its surroundings
questions.explanation: Adiabatic means q = 0, so the change in internal energy equals the work done.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For the isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the change in internal energy ΔU is
questions.explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, and temperature is constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of carbon is -393.5 kJ/mol. How much heat is released when 6 g of carbon burns completely? (C = 12)
questions.explanation: 6 g is 0.5 mol, so heat released = 0.5 × 393.5 = 196.75 kJ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = -40 kJ and ΔS = -100 J/K at 298 K. What is ΔG at this temperature?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS = -40 000 - 298(-100) = -40 000 + 29 800 = -10 200 J, so the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For which of the following reactions is the entropy change positive?
questions.explanation: The decomposition produces a gas from a solid, so disorder increases; the other reactions reduce the number of gas molecules.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Hess's law of constant heat summation.
questions.answer: The total enthalpy change for a reaction is the same whether it occurs in one step or in several steps, because enthalpy is a state function.
keyPoints: Depends only on initial and final states
Because enthalpy is a state function
questions.explanation: This lets us calculate enthalpies of reactions that cannot be measured directly.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction has a negative ΔH and a positive ΔS. Is it spontaneous at all temperatures? Explain.
questions.answer: Yes. ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, and with ΔH negative and ΔS positive both terms make ΔG negative at every temperature.
keyPoints: -TΔS is negative when ΔS is positive
So ΔG is negative at all temperatures
questions.explanation: Both the enthalpy and entropy factors favour the reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On the pH scale at 25 °C, the usual range of values for aqueous solutions is
questions.explanation: pH = 0 for 1 M strong acid and 14 for 1 M strong base, so the scale runs from 0 to 14.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to Arrhenius, a base produces which ion in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Arrhenius defined acids as H+ producers and bases as OH- producers in water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of the ionic product of water, Kw, at 25 °C?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are the units of Kc for the reaction 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g)?
questions.explanation: Kc = [SO3]^2/([SO2]^2[O2]) has units (mol/L)^(2-3) = (mol/L)^-1, which is L/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An acetate buffer has pKa = 4.75 and a [CH3COONa]/[CH3COOH] ratio of 10. What is its pH?
questions.explanation: By the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, pH = 4.75 + log 10 = 5.75.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A 0.1 M solution of a weak acid HA is 1% dissociated. What is the value of Ka?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the common ion effect? Give an example.
questions.answer: The dissociation of a weak electrolyte is suppressed when a strong electrolyte with an ion in common is added; for example, NH4Cl added to NH4OH lowers the OH- concentration.
keyPoints: Added ion is common to the weak electrolyte
Equilibrium shifts toward the undissociated form
Example: NH4Cl with NH4OH, or sodium acetate with acetic acid
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, extra NH4+ pushes the ionisation of NH3 backwards.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For X ⇌ Y, Kc = 4 at a certain temperature. If a mixture has [X] = 1 M and [Y] = 8 M, in which direction will the reaction proceed to reach equilibrium?
questions.answer: Backward (towards X), because Qc = 8 is greater than Kc = 4.
keyPoints: Net reaction goes from products to reactants
questions.explanation: When Qc exceeds Kc, there is too much product and the system shifts backward.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The rusting of iron is an example of
questions.explanation: Iron loses electrons and is oxidised, forming hydrated iron(III) oxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of an element in its free (uncombined) state?
questions.explanation: In an elemental substance all atoms are identical, so there is no electron transfer and the oxidation number is zero.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in the ammonium ion, NH4+?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in the manganate ion, MnO4 2-?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2KI + Cl2 → 2KCl + I2, the iodide ion is
questions.explanation: I- loses electrons to become I2 (oxidation number -1 to 0), so it is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species can act only as an oxidising agent and never as a reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Mn in MnO4- is already in its highest oxidation state (+7), so it can only be reduced.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of change in oxidation number, and illustrate with CuO + H2 → Cu + H2O.
questions.answer: Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number and reduction is a decrease. In the reaction, H2 is oxidised (0 to +1) and Cu in CuO is reduced (+2 to 0).
questions.explanation: Both processes occur together, which makes the reaction a redox reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Show that the reaction Cl2 + 2OH- → Cl- + ClO- + H2O is a disproportionation reaction.
questions.answer: Chlorine goes from 0 in Cl2 to -1 in Cl- (reduction) and to +1 in ClO- (oxidation), so the same element is both oxidised and reduced.
questions.explanation: A reaction in which one species is simultaneously oxidised and reduced is called disproportionation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which element is the most abundant in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen makes up about 70% of the mass of the universe.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The general outer electronic configuration of alkali metals is
questions.explanation: Alkali metals (group 1) have a single electron in the outermost s orbital.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of baking soda?
