questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (sodium bicarbonate), NaHCO3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Milk of lime is
options: a suspension of calcium hydroxide in water
questions.explanation: Slaked lime is only sparingly soluble, and its suspension in water is called milk of lime.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Sodium metal is manufactured commercially by
questions.explanation: In Down's process molten NaCl (with CaCl2 added to lower the melting point) is electrolysed and sodium forms at the cathode.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following hydroxides is the strongest base?
questions.explanation: Basic character of group 2 hydroxides increases down the group, so Ba(OH)2 is strongest and Be(OH)2 is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Potassium burns in excess oxygen to give the superoxide KO2, whereas lithium gives only Li2O. This is because
options: potassium has a smaller ionic radius than lithium
a large cation like K+ stabilises the large superoxide ion, but the small Li+ cannot
lithium has a higher atomic number
questions.explanation: Large anions are stabilised by large cations of low charge density, so K, Rb and Cs form superoxides.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate and name the products.
questions.answer: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 on strong heating (about 1200 K). The products are quicklime (calcium oxide) and carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: This reaction is used industrially to make lime from limestone.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is the first ionisation enthalpy of an alkaline earth metal higher than that of the alkali metal in the same period?
questions.answer: Alkaline earth atoms are smaller and have a greater nuclear charge, so the outer electron is held more strongly.
questions.explanation: For example, Mg has a higher first ionisation enthalpy than Na.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 13 elements?
questions.explanation: Group 13 elements have three valence electrons, two in the s and one in the p subshell.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond has a rigid three-dimensional covalent network of sp3 carbon atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On strong heating, boric acid finally gives
questions.explanation: H3BO3 loses water to form metaboric acid HBO2 and then boron trioxide, B2O3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The two common oxidation states shown by group 14 elements are
questions.explanation: Group 14 elements have four valence electrons, giving +4 mainly and +2 (more stable for heavier members) through the inert pair effect.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is neutral?
questions.explanation: CO does not react with acids or bases; CO2 and SiO2 are acidic and SnO2 is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Boron trifluoride readily forms an addition compound with ammonia because
options: BF3 is a strong reducing agent
BF3 is electron-deficient and accepts the lone pair of NH3
questions.explanation: Boron in BF3 has only six electrons, so it acts as a Lewis acid and forms the coordinate adduct H3N→BF3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Thallium shows the +1 oxidation state more readily than +3. This is due to
questions.explanation: In the heaviest group 13 element the 6s2 pair is reluctant to take part in bonding, which stabilises the lower oxidation state.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Mention two uses of borax.
questions.answer: Borax is used in making heat-resistant borosilicate glass and enamels, and as a flux in soldering and welding; it is also used in the borax bead test.
questions.explanation: On heating, borax gives a glassy bead of sodium metaborate and boron trioxide that dissolves metal oxides.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Diamond is extremely hard, while graphite is soft and used as a lubricant. Explain the difference.
questions.answer: In diamond every carbon is bonded tetrahedrally to four others in a strong 3D network. In graphite carbon atoms are in layers held together by weak van der Waals forces, so the layers slide over one another.
keyPoints: Diamond: rigid 3D network of sp3 carbons
Weak forces between graphite layers allow sliding
questions.explanation: The structure explains the different mechanical properties of the two allotropes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is a hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen, which is true only for C2H6 (ethane).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to a saturated carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CHO?
questions.explanation: Two carbons with an aldehyde group give ethanal (acetaldehyde).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many structural isomers does pentane, C5H12, have (including itself)?
questions.explanation: The isomers are pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkyl groups has the strongest +I effect?
questions.explanation: The +I effect increases with the number of alkyl groups on the carbon, so tert-butyl is strongest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Steam distillation is used to purify organic compounds that are
options: steam volatile and immiscible with water
questions.explanation: Such compounds, for example aniline, distil with steam at a temperature below their own boiling point and can be separated from the water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Kjeldahl's method, the ammonia obtained from 1.4 g of an organic compound neutralised 20 mL of 1 M H2SO4. What is the percentage of nitrogen in the compound? (N = 14)
questions.explanation: 20 mL of 1 M H2SO4 is 0.02 mol, which neutralises 0.04 mol NH3; 0.04 × 14 = 0.56 g N, and 0.56/1.4 × 100 = 40%.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define homologous series and give one example.
questions.answer: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a -CH2- unit; example: methane, ethane, propane (alkanes).
questions.explanation: Members share a general formula and show a gradual change in physical properties.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol.
questions.answer: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by delocalisation of its negative charge into the benzene ring through resonance, whereas the ethoxide ion has no such stabilisation and the alkyl group even destabilises it.
keyPoints: More stable conjugate base means stronger acid
questions.explanation: The more stable the conjugate base, the more easily the proton is lost.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the H-C-C bond angle in ethyne, HC≡CH?
questions.explanation: Each carbon is sp hybridised, so the molecule is linear.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethane has only single bonds, whereas the others have double, triple or aromatic bonding.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Cracking of alkanes is the process of
options: breaking larger alkane molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes by heating
questions.explanation: Heating higher alkanes at high temperature, with or without a catalyst, splits them into smaller hydrocarbons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the chlorination of methane in sunlight, the step Cl2 → 2Cl• is called
questions.explanation: Initiation produces the free radicals that start the chain reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many different monochloro structural isomers can be obtained from propane?
questions.explanation: 1-Chloropropane and 2-chloropropane are possible, because propane has two kinds of hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Nitration of toluene (methylbenzene) gives mainly
questions.explanation: The methyl group is an activating, ortho/para directing substituent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethene reacts with cold dilute alkaline potassium permanganate solution to give
questions.explanation: Baeyer's reagent adds two hydroxyl groups across the double bond, and the purple colour is discharged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the preparation of methane by heating sodium acetate with soda lime.
questions.explanation: The carboxylate group is lost as carbonate, leaving the methyl group to take a hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why is the staggered conformation of ethane more stable than the eclipsed conformation?
questions.answer: In the staggered form the C-H bonds on the two carbons are as far apart as possible, so there is minimum repulsion (torsional strain); in the eclipsed form they are closest, giving the highest repulsion.
keyPoints: Eclipsed: bond pairs closest, maximum torsional strain
questions.explanation: The lower energy of the staggered form means ethane spends most of its time in it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the unit of molarity?
questions.explanation: Molarity is moles of solute per litre of solution, so its unit is mol per litre.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the SI base unit of mass?
questions.explanation: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass; the litre is not an SI base unit and metre and kelvin measure length and temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the mass of one atom of carbon-12 in grams? (NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the molecular mass of glucose, C6H12O6? (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage of nitrogen by mass in urea, CO(NH2)2? (C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O, what mass of NO is formed from 17 g of NH3 with excess oxygen? (N = 14, O = 16, H = 1)
questions.explanation: 17 g of NH3 is 1 mol, and 4 mol NH3 gives 4 mol NO, so 1 mol NO = 30 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 100 mL of 0.2 M HCl is mixed with 100 mL of 0.4 M HCl. What is the molarity of the resulting solution?
questions.explanation: Total moles = 0.02 + 0.04 = 0.06 mol in 0.2 L, giving 0.3 M.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define mole fraction and calculate the mole fraction of ethanol in a mixture of 1 mol ethanol and 4 mol water.
questions.answer: Mole fraction of a component is its moles divided by the total moles of all components; for ethanol it is 1/(1 + 4) = 0.2.
keyPoints: Mole fraction = moles of component / total moles
questions.explanation: Mole fractions of all components add up to 1, so water is 0.8.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A hydrocarbon contains 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass and has a molar mass of 42 g/mol. Find its molecular formula.
questions.explanation: The molecular formula is the empirical formula multiplied by the ratio of molar mass to empirical formula mass.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Who discovered the neutron?
questions.explanation: Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The plum pudding model of the atom was proposed by
questions.explanation: Thomson proposed that electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere, like plums in a pudding.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many electrons are present in the 3d subshell of an iron atom (Z = 26) in the ground state?
questions.explanation: The configuration of iron is [Ar] 3d6 4s2, so there are six 3d electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a 4f subshell?
questions.explanation: An f subshell has 7 orbitals, each holding 2 electrons, so 14 in total.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to Bohr's model, the angular momentum of an electron in a stationary orbit is
questions.explanation: Bohr's quantisation condition is mvr = nh/2π, with n = 1, 2, 3 and so on.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the frequency of light of wavelength 600 nm? (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons in an atom that can have the quantum numbers n = 3 and ml = +1?
questions.explanation: ml = +1 occurs in the 3p subshell and the 3d subshell, giving two orbitals, which hold 4 electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between an orbit and an orbital.
questions.answer: An orbit is a fixed circular path of an electron around the nucleus in Bohr's model; an orbital is a three-dimensional region around the nucleus where the probability of finding an electron is high, described by a wave function.
keyPoints: Orbital: region of probability from quantum mechanics
An orbital holds at most two electrons
questions.explanation: The orbital concept follows from the uncertainty principle, which does not allow definite paths.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A photon has an energy of 4.97 × 10^-19 J. Calculate its wavelength. (h = 6.626 × 10^-34 J s, c = 3 × 10^8 m/s)
questions.explanation: The wavelength lies at the violet end of the visible spectrum.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many elements are there in the second period of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: The second period runs from lithium to neon, which is 8 elements.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The lanthanoids belong to which block?
questions.explanation: In lanthanoids the 4f subshell is being filled, so they are f-block elements.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the alkali metals Li, Na, K and Cs has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Ionisation enthalpy decreases down a group as atomic size increases, so lithium has the highest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which halogen is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid and iodine is a solid at room temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ions is isoelectronic with argon?
questions.explanation: Argon has 18 electrons, and Ca2+ (20 - 2 = 18) has the same number.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following oxides is the most acidic?
questions.explanation: Acidic character of oxides increases across a period, and Cl2O7 is a strongly acidic oxide of a non-metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Atomic size decreases across a period from left to right mainly because
options: the effective nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell
electrons are removed from the atoms
questions.explanation: Each step adds one proton and one electron in the same shell, so the pull on outer electrons strengthens.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are isoelectronic species? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Atoms or ions with the same number of electrons; for example Na+ and Mg2+ (and F- and Ne), which all have 10 electrons.
keyPoints: Examples: O2-, F-, Ne, Na+, Mg2+
questions.explanation: In an isoelectronic series, radius decreases as nuclear charge increases.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The electron gain enthalpy of fluorine is less negative than that of chlorine. Explain.
questions.answer: The fluorine atom is very small, so the added electron enters a compact 2p subshell where strong electron-electron repulsion reduces the energy released.
keyPoints: Fluorine has a very small 2p subshell
Chlorine's larger 3p subshell accommodates the electron more easily
questions.explanation: Hence chlorine has the most negative electron gain enthalpy of all the elements.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An electrovalent (ionic) bond is usually formed between
questions.explanation: Metals of low ionisation enthalpy lose electrons to non-metals of high electron gain enthalpy, forming ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following diatomic molecules contains a triple bond?
questions.explanation: N2 has the structure N≡N, with one sigma and two pi bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of the sulphur dioxide molecule, SO2?
questions.explanation: Sulphur has two bond pairs and one lone pair (sp2), giving a bent molecule.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the hydrogen halides HF, HCl, HBr and HI has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: HF forms strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which raise its boiling point above the others.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the hybridisation of sulphur in SF6?
questions.explanation: Six bond pairs around sulphur require six hybrid orbitals, giving an octahedral sp3d2 arrangement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many lone pairs are present on the nitrogen atom in ammonia, NH3?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has five valence electrons; three form N-H bonds and the other two form one lone pair.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of species has the same shape (is isostructural)?
questions.explanation: Both NH3 and H3O+ have three bond pairs and one lone pair on the central atom, so both are pyramidal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Define dipole moment and give its common unit.
questions.answer: Dipole moment is the product of the magnitude of the charge and the distance between the charges in a polar bond or molecule; its common unit is the debye (D).
questions.explanation: Molecules with zero net dipole moment, such as CO2, are non-polar even if their bonds are polar.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Explain why BF3 is planar while NH3 is pyramidal.
questions.answer: Boron in BF3 has three bond pairs and no lone pair (sp2, trigonal planar), whereas nitrogen in NH3 has three bond pairs and one lone pair (sp3), which pushes the bonds into a pyramidal shape.
keyPoints: BF3: three bond pairs, no lone pair, sp2
NH3: three bond pairs plus one lone pair, sp3
Lone pair repulsion distorts NH3 from tetrahedral to pyramidal
questions.explanation: The number of lone pairs on the central atom determines the molecular shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gases is the easiest to liquefy?
questions.explanation: CO2 has strong intermolecular attractions and a high critical temperature, so it liquefies readily, unlike the very weakly attracting He, H2 and Ne.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At 273 K and 1 atm, one mole of an ideal gas occupies approximately
questions.explanation: The molar volume at 273 K and 1 atm is 22.4 L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas at 1 atm occupies 4 L. At constant temperature it is compressed to 2 L. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, P2 = P1V1/V2 = 1 × 4/2 = 2 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas in a rigid container has a pressure of 2 atm at 300 K. What is its pressure at 450 K?
questions.explanation: At constant volume P is proportional to T, so P2 = 2 × 450/300 = 3 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the van der Waals equation, the constant 'a' is a measure of
options: the magnitude of the attractive forces between gas molecules
the volume of one mole of molecules
the number of molecules in the gas
questions.explanation: The term a n^2/V^2 corrects for intermolecular attractions, so a larger 'a' means stronger attractions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At the same temperature, how many times greater is the root mean square speed of H2 molecules than that of O2 molecules?
questions.explanation: u_rms is proportional to 1/sqrt(M), so the ratio is sqrt(32/2) = 4.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The surface tension of a liquid decreases when the temperature is raised because
options: the kinetic energy of molecules increases and the effective intermolecular attraction weakens
questions.explanation: Greater molecular motion reduces the net inward pull on surface molecules, so surface tension falls.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Charles's law.
questions.answer: At constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V/T = constant).
keyPoints: Pressure and amount of gas constant
V is directly proportional to T
questions.explanation: Extrapolating the graph of V against T gives zero volume at -273.15 °C.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the volume occupied by 2.2 g of carbon dioxide at 300 K and 1 atm, assuming ideal behaviour. (C = 12, O = 16; R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)
questions.explanation: Substituting into the ideal gas equation gives 1.23 L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which thermodynamic quantity is a measure of the disorder of a system?
questions.explanation: Entropy measures the randomness or disorder of a system.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In an exothermic reaction carried out in an open container, the temperature of the surroundings
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so their temperature rises.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of liquid water is -286 kJ/mol. What is the enthalpy change for 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l)?
questions.explanation: The equation forms 2 mol of water, so ΔH = 2 × (-286) = -572 kJ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A system loses 50 J of heat and has 30 J of work done on it. What is ΔU?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A gas expands from 1 L to 4 L against a constant external pressure of 2 atm. What is the work done on the gas?
questions.explanation: w = -P ΔV = -2 × (4 - 1) = -6 L atm, negative because the gas does work on the surroundings.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A reaction has a positive ΔH and a negative ΔS. Its spontaneity is
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS has a positive ΔH and a positive -TΔS, so ΔG is positive at every temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The burning of 1.0 g of a fuel in a calorimeter raises the temperature of 500 g of water by 10 K. How much heat is absorbed by the water? (specific heat of water = 4.18 J g^-1 K^-1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is meant by the standard enthalpy of formation of a compound?
questions.answer: It is the enthalpy change when one mole of the compound is formed from its elements in their most stable states under standard conditions (1 bar pressure, usually 298 K).
keyPoints: One mole of the compound formed
From elements in their standard states
questions.explanation: By convention the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state is zero.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State the second law of thermodynamics in terms of entropy and use it to explain why heat flows from a hot body to a cold body.
questions.answer: The entropy of the universe increases in every spontaneous process. When heat flows from hot to cold, the entropy gained by the cold body exceeds the entropy lost by the hot body, so the total entropy rises.
keyPoints: Total entropy of universe increases in spontaneous change
Entropy change q/T is larger for the cold body
questions.explanation: Since the same heat q is divided by a lower temperature for the cold body, its entropy gain is greater.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At chemical equilibrium
options: the concentrations of reactants and products are equal
the rates of the forward and backward reactions are equal
all the reactants have been used up
questions.explanation: Equilibrium is dynamic: both reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: HCl ionises almost completely in water, whereas the other three are weak acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of 0.05 M sulphuric acid, assuming that both hydrogen ions ionise completely?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of which salt is acidic?
questions.explanation: NH4+ is the conjugate acid of a weak base and hydrolyses to give H3O+, while Cl- does not hydrolyse.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the conjugate acid of ammonia, NH3?
questions.explanation: NH3 accepts a proton to form NH4+, its conjugate acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The molar solubility of Ca(OH)2 in water is 1 × 10^-3 M. What is its solubility product, Ksp?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g), what happens to the amount of PCl5 at equilibrium if extra Cl2 is added at constant temperature?
questions.explanation: Adding a product shifts the equilibrium backward, forming more PCl5.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State Le Chatelier's principle.
questions.answer: If a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, pressure or temperature, the equilibrium shifts in the direction that tends to counteract the change.
keyPoints: Applies to a system at equilibrium
Change in concentration, pressure or temperature
Equilibrium shifts to oppose the change
questions.explanation: It allows us to predict how conditions change the yield, for example in the Haber process.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the pH of the solution obtained by mixing 100 mL of 0.2 M HCl with 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH.
keyPoints: Excess H+ = 0.01 mol in 0.2 L = 0.05 M
questions.explanation: The strong base neutralises half the acid, leaving 0.05 M H+.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of hydrogen in most of its compounds with non-metals?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is +1 in compounds with non-metals and -1 only in metal hydrides.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In any redox reaction, the number of electrons lost by the reducing agent is
options: equal to the number of electrons gained by the oxidising agent
questions.explanation: Electrons are conserved: those released in oxidation are taken up in reduction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of phosphorus in H3PO4?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of carbon in methanol, CH3OH?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Oxidising power of the halogens decreases down the group, and fluorine is the strongest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: Magnesium changes from 0 to +2 and oxygen from 0 to -2, while the others involve no change of oxidation numbers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which element is oxidised in Cu + 2AgNO3 → Cu(NO3)2 + 2Ag?
questions.explanation: Copper changes from 0 to +2, so it loses electrons and is oxidised.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is a half-reaction? Write the oxidation half-reaction for zinc metal turning into zinc ions.
questions.answer: A half-reaction shows either the oxidation or the reduction part of a redox reaction separately, with the electrons; for zinc: Zn → Zn2+ + 2e-.
keyPoints: Shows only the oxidation or only the reduction
questions.explanation: Adding the oxidation and reduction half-reactions gives the overall redox equation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2, identify the oxidising agent and the reducing agent with the changes in oxidation number.
questions.answer: Fe2O3 is the oxidising agent (Fe goes from +3 to 0); CO is the reducing agent (C goes from +2 to +4).
keyPoints: Fe2O3 is oxidising agent, CO reducing agent
questions.explanation: This is the key reaction in the blast furnace extraction of iron.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the lightest metal?
questions.explanation: Lithium has a density of about 0.53 g/cm3, the lowest of all metals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Alkali metals are strong reducing agents because
options: they readily lose their single valence electron
they have very small atomic sizes
questions.explanation: Their low ionisation enthalpies make them lose electrons easily, which reduces other substances.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What flame colour does a potassium compound give?
questions.explanation: Potassium gives a lilac flame; sodium is golden yellow, calcium brick red and lithium crimson.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
questions.explanation: Gypsum is calcium sulphate dihydrate, CaSO4·2H2O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen peroxide is stored in dark or plastic bottles because it
options: decomposes in light to give water and oxygen
reacts with glass to form hydrogen
questions.explanation: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2 is accelerated by light, and traces of alkali from glass also speed it up.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an electron-deficient hydride?
questions.explanation: B2H6 has too few electrons to form normal two-centre bonds for all its atoms, whereas CH4 is electron-precise and NH3 and H2O are electron-rich.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is plaster of Paris? Write the equation for its setting with water.
questions.answer: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO4·1/2 H2O. On mixing with water it sets to gypsum: CaSO4·1/2 H2O + 1 1/2 H2O → CaSO4·2H2O.
keyPoints: Made by heating gypsum at about 393 K
questions.explanation: It is used for plastering fractured bones and for making moulds and statues.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Lithium chloride is soluble in organic solvents but sodium chloride is not. Explain.
questions.answer: The small Li+ ion has high polarising power, so LiCl has considerable covalent character according to Fajans' rules and dissolves in less polar solvents; NaCl is almost purely ionic.
keyPoints: Li+ is very small with high charge density
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds dissolve in organic solvents, while ionic ones do not.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The chief ore of aluminium is
questions.explanation: Bauxite, Al2O3·2H2O, is the main ore of aluminium; cryolite is used only to lower the melting point in electrolysis.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which allotrope of carbon consists of football-shaped molecules?
questions.explanation: Buckminsterfullerene, C60, has 60 carbon atoms arranged in a cage like a football.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: On heating in the borax bead test, borax first gives
questions.explanation: Na2B4O7 → 2NaBO2 + B2O3, forming a transparent glassy bead that is used for detecting metals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many oxygen atoms is each silicon atom bonded to in the structure of silicon dioxide?
questions.explanation: In SiO2 each silicon is tetrahedrally bonded to four oxygen atoms in a giant network.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Water gas is a mixture of
questions.explanation: Water gas, made by passing steam over red-hot coke, consists of carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: CO2 is a gas while SiO2 is a hard solid with a very high melting point because
options: silicon is more electronegative than carbon
CO2 consists of discrete molecules with weak forces between them, whereas SiO2 is a giant covalent network
questions.explanation: Melting SiO2 requires breaking strong covalent bonds throughout the network, but CO2 only needs weak intermolecular forces overcome.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What are silicones? Mention two uses.
questions.answer: Silicones are organosilicon polymers with a repeating -R2Si-O- chain. They are used as lubricants and sealants, in water-proofing materials and in medical implants.
keyPoints: Polymers with Si-O-Si backbone and organic groups
questions.explanation: They are made by hydrolysis and condensation of alkyl chlorosilanes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Show with equations that aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric.
questions.answer: With acid: Al(OH)3 + 3HCl → AlCl3 + 3H2O. With alkali: Al(OH)3 + NaOH → Na[Al(OH)4]. It behaves as a base with acids and as an acid with bases.
keyPoints: Reacts with HCl to give salt and water
Reacts with NaOH to give sodium tetrahydroxoaluminate
questions.explanation: A substance reacting with both acids and bases is called amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an alkene?
questions.explanation: C2H4 (ethene) contains a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is an alkene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A carbon atom forming four single bonds is
questions.explanation: Four sigma bonds around carbon need four equivalent hybrid orbitals, so it is sp3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3CH2COOH?
questions.explanation: Three carbons including the carboxyl carbon give propanoic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The reaction CH3Cl + OH- → CH3OH + Cl- is an example of
questions.explanation: The nucleophile OH- replaces the chloride leaving group on carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following shows geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: In but-2-ene each double-bonded carbon has two different groups (H and CH3), so cis and trans forms exist.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol and dimethyl ether, both C2H6O, are examples of
questions.explanation: One has an -OH group (alcohol) and the other an ether group, so they are functional isomers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons with one example each.
questions.answer: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single C-C bonds (for example ethane), whereas unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one double or triple carbon-carbon bond (for example ethene or ethyne).
keyPoints: Saturated: only single bonds, e.g. ethane
Unsaturated: C=C or C≡C present, e.g. ethene
questions.explanation: Unsaturated compounds undergo addition reactions, unlike saturated ones.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Why are the two carbon-oxygen bonds in the acetate ion, CH3COO-, equal in length?
questions.answer: The negative charge is delocalised over both oxygen atoms through resonance, so each C-O bond has partial double-bond character and the bonds are identical.
keyPoints: Bond length intermediate between C-O and C=O
questions.explanation: The real structure is a resonance hybrid, not either single drawn structure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following alkanes is a gas at room temperature?
questions.explanation: The first four straight-chain alkanes (C1 to C4) are gases at room temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the general formula of the alkyne series?
questions.explanation: Alkynes with one triple bond have the formula CnH2n-2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Hydration of ethyne with dilute H2SO4 and HgSO4 gives
questions.explanation: The initial vinyl alcohol is unstable and rearranges (tautomerises) to ethanal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzene reacts with chloromethane in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 to give
questions.explanation: This Friedel-Crafts alkylation puts a methyl group on the ring, forming methylbenzene (toluene).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A mixture of CH3Cl and C2H5Cl is heated with sodium in dry ether. How many different alkanes can be formed?
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction can couple like or unlike groups, giving ethane (CH3-CH3), propane (CH3-C2H5) and butane (C2H5-C2H5).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzene reacts with chlorine in bright sunlight (UV) without a catalyst to give mainly
questions.explanation: Under UV light chlorine adds across the ring by a free radical mechanism, giving 1,2,3,4,5,6-hexachlorocyclohexane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the reaction of ethene with bromine and state what is observed.
questions.answer: CH2=CH2 + Br2 → CH2Br-CH2Br (1,2-dibromoethane). The reddish-brown colour of bromine is discharged.
keyPoints: Electrophilic addition across the double bond
questions.explanation: This decolourisation is used as a test for unsaturation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Arrange n-pentane, isopentane and neopentane in increasing order of boiling point and explain.
questions.answer: Neopentane < isopentane < n-pentane. Branching makes the molecule more compact, which reduces surface area and so van der Waals forces.
keyPoints: Weaker dispersion forces mean lower boiling point
questions.explanation: The straight-chain isomer has the largest contact area between molecules and therefore the highest boiling point.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: One mole of any substance contains
questions.explanation: A mole contains Avogadro's number, 6.022 × 10^23, of atoms, molecules or ions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 10 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 90 g of water. What is the mass percent of sodium chloride in the solution?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the mass of 3.011 × 10^23 molecules of water? (H2O = 18 g/mol; NA = 6.022 × 10^23 per mol)
questions.explanation: 3.011 × 10^23 molecules is 0.5 mol, so mass = 0.5 × 18 = 9 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What volume of 0.2 M NaOH solution is needed to neutralise 20 mL of 0.1 M HCl?
questions.explanation: Moles of HCl = 0.020 × 0.1 = 0.002 mol, and the volume of 0.2 M NaOH = 0.002/0.2 = 0.01 L = 10 mL.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: 10 g of calcium carbonate is heated and gives 5.6 g of calcium oxide. By the law of conservation of mass, what mass of carbon dioxide is released?
questions.explanation: Mass of reactant equals mass of products, so CO2 = 10 - 5.6 = 4.4 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A 1.22 g sample of hydrated barium chloride, BaCl2·xH2O, loses 0.18 g of water on heating. What is x? (Ba = 137, Cl = 35.5, H2O = 18)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The nucleus of an atom contains
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons (nucleons), while electrons move outside it.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The spectral series of hydrogen that lies in the visible region is the
questions.explanation: The Balmer series, which ends at n = 2, has lines in the visible region.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Lyman series of the hydrogen spectrum lies in which region?
questions.explanation: Lyman lines arise from transitions to n = 1 and involve the largest energy gaps, which gives ultraviolet radiation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many radial nodes does a 2s orbital have?
questions.explanation: Radial nodes = n - l - 1 = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the shape of a p orbital?
questions.explanation: A p orbital has two lobes on opposite sides of the nucleus, which gives a dumb-bell shape.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following electron configurations is impossible?
questions.explanation: The 2p subshell has 3 orbitals, so by the Pauli exclusion principle it can hold at most 6 electrons, not 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Silicon has properties between those of metals and non-metals, so it is a metalloid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The elements of group 17 are called
questions.explanation: Group 17 (F, Cl, Br, I, At) elements are the halogens.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the elements Be, Mg, Ca and Ba has the highest metallic character?
questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group, so barium is the most metallic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements of the third period has the largest atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period, so sodium at the left end is the largest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Beryllium resembles aluminium (a diagonal relationship). Which property do both elements share?
options: Both form amphoteric oxides and hydroxides
Both have the same atomic radius
questions.explanation: BeO and Al2O3 are amphoteric, and both metals form covalent chlorides and are rendered passive by concentrated nitric acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the elements Mg, Al, Na and Si has the highest second ionisation enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Removing the second electron from Na+ breaks the stable noble gas core 2s2 2p6, which needs far more energy than removing the second electron from the others.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which carbon-carbon bond has the highest bond enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Bond enthalpy increases with bond order, and the triple bond is strongest.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The bond between hydrogen and chlorine in HCl is
questions.explanation: The electrons are shared unequally because chlorine is more electronegative than hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the H-C-H bond angle in methane?
questions.explanation: The four sp3 bonds point to the corners of a regular tetrahedron, at 109.5 degrees.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following molecules does the central atom have an incomplete octet?
questions.explanation: Boron in BF3 has only six electrons around it, while the central atoms in the others have eight.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of valence electrons in one molecule of ammonia, NH3?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen contributes 5 and three hydrogens contribute 1 each, giving 8.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is non-polar although it contains polar bonds?
questions.explanation: CCl4 is tetrahedral and symmetrical, so its four C-Cl bond dipoles cancel.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the value of 1 atm in pascal?
questions.explanation: 1 atm = 101 325 Pa, or about 1.013 × 10^5 Pa.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Water rises in a narrow glass capillary tube because of
options: surface tension and the adhesion of water to the glass
questions.explanation: Adhesion between water and glass is stronger than cohesion in water, and surface tension pulls the liquid up the tube.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Evaporation of a liquid causes cooling because
options: heat is added to the surroundings
the most energetic molecules escape, lowering the average kinetic energy of the rest
questions.explanation: Only the fastest molecules can leave the surface, so the average kinetic energy, and hence temperature, of the liquid drops.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is 25 °C expressed on the kelvin scale?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: At the same temperature and pressure, what is the ratio of the density of oxygen gas to that of hydrogen gas?
questions.explanation: At the same T and P, density is proportional to molar mass, so 32/2 = 16.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What volume is occupied by 0.5 mol of an ideal gas at 2 atm and 300 K? (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the unit of molar entropy?
questions.explanation: Entropy has units of energy per kelvin, so molar entropy is J K^-1 mol^-1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A calorimeter is used to measure
options: heat changes in chemical or physical processes
questions.explanation: A calorimeter measures the heat absorbed or released in a reaction, from the temperature change of a known mass of water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of a substance is always
options: dependent on the sign of ΔS
questions.explanation: Combustion releases heat, so the enthalpy change is negative.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What standard pressure is used for thermodynamic data under the current IUPAC recommendation?
questions.explanation: The standard state pressure is 1 bar (10^5 Pa).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has the highest molar entropy?
questions.explanation: Gases are the most disordered state, so steam has the highest entropy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The enthalpy of atomisation of methane, CH4(g) → C(g) + 4H(g), is 1660 kJ/mol. What is the average C-H bond enthalpy?
questions.explanation: Four C-H bonds are broken, so the average bond enthalpy = 1660/4 = 415 kJ/mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g), the difference ΔH - ΔU is
questions.explanation: Δng = 1 - 1 = 0, so ΔH = ΔU + ΔngRT = ΔU.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid is
questions.explanation: A Brønsted-Lowry acid donates a proton (H+) to another species.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: In pure water [H+] = 10^-7 M, so pH = 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A solution of pH 3 has how many times the hydrogen ion concentration of a solution of pH 5?
questions.explanation: pH differs by 2 units, so the [H+] differs by 10^2 = 100 times.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A very large value of Kc for a reaction means that at equilibrium
options: reactants and products are present in equal amounts
questions.explanation: Kc is the ratio of product to reactant concentrations, so a large Kc means the reaction goes nearly to completion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following mixtures acts as an alkaline buffer?
questions.explanation: A weak base with its salt with a strong acid resists changes in pH on the alkaline side.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), the relation between Kp and Kc is
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc (RT)^Δng and Δng = 2 - 4 = -2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The Ksp of AgCl is 1.8 × 10^-10. What is its solubility in 0.1 M NaCl solution (ignoring the Cl- from AgCl)?
questions.explanation: [Ag+] = Ksp/[Cl-] = 1.8 × 10^-10 / 0.1 = 1.8 × 10^-9 M, far lower than in pure water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of sodium in NaCl?
questions.explanation: Alkali metals always have an oxidation number of +1 in their compounds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: An oxidising agent
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent takes electrons from another species and is itself reduced.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of chlorine in sodium hypochlorite, NaClO?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in nitric acid, HNO3?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions will take place?
questions.explanation: Iron is above copper in the activity series, so it displaces copper; the other reactions would need a less reactive metal to displace a more reactive one.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following compounds does nitrogen have the oxidation number +4?
questions.explanation: The oxidation numbers of nitrogen are +4 in NO2, +1 in N2O, +2 in NO and +5 in N2O5.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In acidic solution, how many moles of KMnO4 are needed to oxidise 5 mol of Fe2+ to Fe3+?
questions.explanation: Each MnO4- accepts 5 electrons (Mn +7 to +2), and each Fe2+ gives 1 electron, so 5 mol Fe2+ needs 1 mol MnO4-.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which is the most abundant isotope of hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Protium (1H) makes up over 99.98% of natural hydrogen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which alkali metal has a melting point close to room temperature (about 28.5 °C)?
questions.explanation: Caesium has the lowest melting point among the alkali metals and melts just above room temperature.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of caustic soda?
questions.explanation: Caustic soda is sodium hydroxide, NaOH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Bleaching powder is prepared by passing chlorine gas over
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → Ca(OCl)Cl + H2O, giving bleaching powder (CaOCl2).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which s-block element is present in chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll has a magnesium ion at the centre of its porphyrin ring.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In Clark's method, temporary hardness of water is removed by adding
options: a calculated amount of slaked lime
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)2 reacts with Ca(HCO3)2 to give insoluble CaCO3, which is filtered off.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What volume of hydrogen gas at 273 K and 1 atm is produced when 2.3 g of sodium reacts with excess water? (Na = 23; molar volume 22.4 L/mol)
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2, so 0.1 mol Na gives 0.05 mol H2 = 1.12 L.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: State two ways in which lithium differs from the other alkali metals.
questions.answer: Lithium is harder and has a higher melting point; it forms a nitride with nitrogen and its carbonate, hydroxide and nitrate decompose on heating more easily, and LiCl is deliquescent and soluble in organic solvents.
keyPoints: Compounds are more covalent and less thermally stable
questions.explanation: The differences are due to the very small size and high polarising power of Li+.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is commonly used in fire extinguishers?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is non-combustible and heavier than air, so it smothers fires.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Carborundum is the common name of
questions.explanation: Carborundum is silicon carbide, SiC, an extremely hard abrasive.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Among the boron trihalides, which is the strongest Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: Back bonding is strongest in BF3 (similar-sized 2p orbitals) and weakest in BBr3, so BBr3 is the most electron-deficient and the strongest acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Graphite is used for electrodes because it
questions.explanation: Delocalised electrons between its layers make graphite a good conductor, and it is also chemically inert.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: In the thermite reaction, aluminium acts as
questions.explanation: In 2Al + Fe2O3 → Al2O3 + 2Fe, aluminium is oxidised and reduces the iron(III) oxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The B-F bond length in BF3 is shorter than expected for a single bond because of
options: pπ-pπ back bonding from fluorine to boron
questions.explanation: Fluorine donates a lone pair into boron's empty 2p orbital, giving partial double-bond character.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: SiCl4 fumes in moist air because
options: it is hydrolysed to give HCl and silicic acid
questions.explanation: SiCl4 + 4H2O → Si(OH)4 + 4HCl, and the HCl forms fumes in damp air.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the equation for the laboratory preparation of diborane from boron trifluoride.
keyPoints: Boron trifluoride treated with lithium aluminium hydride
Products include diborane, LiF and AlF3
questions.explanation: The hydride transfers H- ions to boron, forming B2H6.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The unique property of carbon that allows it to form long chains by linking with itself is called
questions.explanation: Catenation is the ability of atoms of the same element to bond together to form chains and rings.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: The -COOH group is the functional group of
questions.explanation: -COOH is the carboxyl group present in carboxylic acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH3-CH=CH2?
questions.explanation: A three-carbon chain with one double bond is propene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a secondary alcohol?
questions.explanation: In propan-2-ol the carbon bearing -OH is attached to two other carbon atoms.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many alpha (adjacent C-H) hydrogens can take part in hyperconjugation in the tert-butyl carbocation, (CH3)3C+?
questions.explanation: The positive carbon is attached to three methyl groups, each with 3 hydrogens, giving 9.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: A carbocation is
questions.explanation: The positively charged carbon has three sigma bonds and an empty p orbital, so it is trigonal planar and sp2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many structural isomers that are alcohols have the molecular formula C4H10O?
questions.explanation: They are butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Distinguish between an electrophile and a nucleophile with one example each.
questions.answer: An electrophile is an electron-deficient species that accepts an electron pair (for example NO2+ or H+), whereas a nucleophile is an electron-rich species that donates an electron pair (for example OH- or CN-).
keyPoints: Electrophile: electron pair acceptor, e.g. NO2+
Nucleophile: electron pair donor, e.g. OH-
questions.explanation: Most polar organic reactions involve a nucleophile attacking an electron-poor carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is the main constituent of natural gas?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mostly methane, usually over 80 to 90 percent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an aromatic hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Benzene has a planar ring with delocalised pi electrons, which makes it aromatic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: How many pi bonds are there in a Kekulé structure of benzene?
questions.explanation: The ring has three alternating C=C double bonds, each containing one pi bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethene reacts with hydrogen in the presence of finely divided nickel to give
questions.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation converts the double bond to a single bond, giving ethane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Ethyne reacts with excess hydrogen in the presence of nickel to give
questions.explanation: Both pi bonds of the triple bond are hydrogenated, giving ethane (ethene is the intermediate).

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Addition of HCl to 2-methylpropene gives mainly
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule the more stable tertiary carbocation forms, so chlorine attaches to the tertiary carbon.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Benzene does not decolourise bromine water because
options: its delocalised pi electron system gives extra stability, so it resists addition
it is insoluble in all liquids
questions.explanation: Addition would destroy the aromatic stabilisation, so benzene reacts only by substitution under suitable catalysis.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.q: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethyne.
keyPoints: Balanced with 4 C, 4 H and 10 O
Burns with a sooty, luminous flame because of high carbon content
questions.explanation: Ethyne burns with a very hot flame, which is used in oxy-acetylene welding.
